concerns.description: Experiment revisions, logical members, attempts and selected artifacts
concerns.rationale: A logical member is distinct from scheduler attempts; collection evidence must identify the selected successful attempt and content digest.

concerns.description: Pinned inputs and declared numerical comparison policy
concerns.rationale: Reproducibility requires explicit tolerance or exact equivalence and versioned environments; invocation alone does not guarantee deterministic results.

concerns.description: Scatter expansion, retries and selection mechanism
concerns.rationale: CWL-style scatter and retry controllers implement native member/attempt concepts while preserving logical identity.

concerns.description: Scheduler arrays, resource classes and artifact storage placement
concerns.rationale: Scheduler task IDs and node placement are realization details; memory and walltime budgets constrain executable allocation.
This fixture exchanges opaque job/artifact contracts without composing differential equations. An external executable alone does not require C or new kernel semantics.

facets.meaning: Reproduction is evaluated using the declared comparison policy and complete provenance.
obligations: Define tolerance, units and nondeterministic reduction treatment in the policy artifact.
Run a real numerical comparison before claiming reproducibility; no executor or comparator was run.

facets.meaning: Large parameter sweeps must bound resource demand and retry work.
obligations: Choose limits from scheduler capacity and workload measurements.
Validate failed, preempted, missing and duplicate attempts without counting the same member twice.

realization.strategy: Scatter logical members, retain attempt evidence and publish a provenance-complete collection under an explicit comparison policy.
realization.placement: CWL-compatible adapter and Slurm-style arrays are possible realizations; CPU/GPU class and artifact store remain allocation choices.
limitations: No CWL runner, Slurm scheduler or numerical program was executed.
No equations or numerical solver semantics are embedded; modeling those would require a separate specialized artifact.

artifacts.claim: Port contract only; no scheduler submission or workflow execution.
Comparison requirements only; no numerical comparator executed.

sources.title: Ptolemy II models of computation
sources.supports: Directors define distinct continuous-time, discrete-event, synchronous/reactive and dataflow laws; typed graph edges alone do not supply them.

sources.title: Arcadia method
sources.supports: Logical architecture versus physical architecture supports keeping semantic ownership independent of processor placement.

sources.title: CWL Workflow specification
sources.supports: WorkflowStep scatter and ScatterFeatureRequirement are execution mechanisms for logical member expansion.

sources.title: Slurm job arrays
sources.supports: Array task identity and requeue behavior do not guarantee task ordering; logical member identity must survive scheduler attempts.

sources.title: Process Run Crate profile
sources.supports: SoftwareApplication and CreateAction object/result/instrument describe retrospective execution evidence; no RO-Crate conformance is claimed.
